text.div:
AlertSince
No NSAIDs: on an anticoagulant, with hypertension2026-11-19
High fall risk: knee brace, walking frame and left-sided weakness2026-11-19

An elderly Swedish visitor slipped on ice and was brought to the emergency department with a painful, swollen left knee. X-ray showed a displaced transverse fracture of the patella. His Swedish patient summary, read before surgery, showed a penicillin allergy and treatment with insulin, a blood-pressure medicine and an oral anticoagulant. The anticoagulant was paused, and the fracture was fixed the next day by open reduction and tension band wiring under spinal anaesthesia, with clindamycin as prophylaxis. The course after surgery was uneventful: plasma glucose 9 to 14 mmol/L on his usual basal insulin with correction doses, haemoglobin 118 g/L, the anticoagulant restarted the evening after surgery. He was mobilised with a walking frame and a hinged knee brace locked in extension. Simulated episode for an invented person.

Oxycodone (ATC N02AA05)active5 mg by mouth when needed, at most 4 times daily, for at most 7 days after discharge2026-11-16New at discharge, short course. Caution: emphysema, age and a high fall risk. No NSAIDs.
Oral anticoagulant (the patient's existing treatment) (ATC B01A)activeUsual dose, restarted the evening after surgery2026-11-17Existing treatment, paused before surgery and restarted. Thromboprophylaxis: no low-molecular-weight heparin was added, because the existing anticoagulant covers it. The Swedish health centre should confirm the dose and the plan at follow-up.
Insulin (the patient's existing treatment) (ATC A10A)activeUsual basal dose; correction doses were given in hospital2026-11-15Existing treatment, continued. Plasma glucose was 9 to 14 mmol/L after surgery. Closer glucose follow-up is recommended while the patient is immobile.
Clindamycin (ATC J01FF01)completed600 mg intravenously, one dose before surgery2026-11-16Surgical prophylaxis, chosen because of the penicillin allergy. Completed.

SubstanceCategoryCriticalityNote
PenicillinmedicationhighKnown from the patient's Swedish patient summary, read through HIP before surgery. Surgical prophylaxis was therefore clindamycin, not a beta-lactam.

ObservationValueDateReference
Haemoglobin118 g/L2026-11-18134-170 g/L
Plasma glucose12.4 mmol/L2026-11-184.0-6.0 mmol/L fasting
Creatinine96 umol/L2026-11-1860-105 umol/L

AssessmentFindingAssessed
Impaired mobilityWalks short distances with a walking frame and the knee brace locked in extension; weight bearing as tolerated. Needs help on stairs. The left-sided weakness after his earlier stroke adds to the fall risk.2026-11-19

PlanRecommendationActivities
Knee rehabilitation after patella fixationRecommendation to the Swedish health centre: enrol the patient in a structured knee rehabilitation programme, with physiotherapy starting within one week of discharge.Knee brace for 6 weeks, locked in extension when walking; Range of motion 0 to 30 degrees in weeks 1 and 2, then increased step by step to 90 degrees by week 6; Isometric quadriceps exercises and straight leg raises from day 1; Wound check and removal of sutures 14 days after surgery; Control X-ray of the knee 6 weeks after surgery
Diabetes follow-up while immobileRecommendation: closer plasma glucose follow-up for the rehabilitation period.Plasma glucose before meals and at bedtime for 2 weeks; Review of the insulin doses by the diabetes nurse within 1 week
Blood pressure follow-upRecommendation: blood pressure was 158/92 mmHg at discharge, with pain. Follow it at home.Home blood pressure once daily for 2 weeks; Review of the blood-pressure treatment when the pain treatment ends
Anticoagulation and thromboprophylaxisRecommendation: continue the existing anticoagulant without interruption; no additional heparin.Confirm the anticoagulant dose and the bleeding risk at the first follow-up

Discharged in a stable condition to travel home to Sweden with an escort. Walks short distances with a walking frame and the knee brace; needs help on stairs. Pain controlled with paracetamol and a short course of oxycodone. The wound is dry. Follow-up at his Swedish health centre within one week.

Discharged to travel home to Sweden; follow-up at the patient's Swedish health centre.
